name: Northvale Council
description: Northvale Council is a fictional UK local council. It is the sample brand for building and testing the engine. It is not a real organisation.
toneOfVoice: Calm, clear and helpful. Talk to residents as neighbours, not customers. Use short sentences and everyday words. Say what is changing, when, and what the resident needs to do. Lead with the useful fact. Be warm without being chatty. Never use jargon, slogans or exclamation marks.
guidelines:
Northvale Council is a fictional local council used to test the video engine.

Writing
- Plain English, reading age 9. Sentences under 15 words where possible.
- Use 'we' for the council and 'you' for the resident.
- Put dates as 3 March 2027. Times as 9am or 5:30pm. Phone numbers in full.
- Every video ends with one clear action and where to do it.

Look
- Vale Blue backgrounds for openings and endings. White or Mist backgrounds for messages.
- Beacon Yellow is for emphasis on Vale Blue only. Never put yellow on white.
- One idea per scene. Leave plenty of space.
- Icons come from one library (Phosphor) at regular weight, in Vale Blue on Mist circles. Use at most one icon per scene, and pick it by meaning: a calendar for dates, a bin for waste.

Voice
- British English voice, calm pace.

do: Lead with what the resident needs to know or do.
Keep each scene to one idea.
Use Vale Blue, white and Mist as the main colours.
Use Beacon Yellow only to emphasise a word or a link on Vale Blue.
End every video with one action and a web address or phone number.
dont: Do not put yellow text on white or Mist.
Do not use exclamation marks, slogans or jargon.
Do not stretch, recolour or redraw the logo.
Do not use more than one icon per scene.
Do not use photos without people's consent.
